objective.statement: Know how long a sharp or flat lasts within a bar.
successCriteria: I know an accidental lasts to the end of the bar.
I know it applies only on its own line or space.
I know the next bar starts afresh.

explanation.text: An accidental changes the note it is written in front of, and it keeps working for any later note on the same line or space in the same bar.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4 with F sharp, G, F and A. The second F has no sign but is still F sharp.

explanation.caption: The F sharp in beat 3 has no sign of its own, but it is still sharp: the first sharp lasts to the end of the bar.

explanation.text: The accidental stops at the bar-line. In the next bar the same note goes back to normal, unless a new sign is written.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 4/4. The F in bar 1 has a sharp. The F in bar 2 has no sign and is a plain F.

explanation.caption: Bar 1 has an F sharp. In bar 2 the F is plain F again.

explanation.text: The accidental belongs to one line or space only. A sharp on this F does not affect an F in a different octave.
Ask two questions: 'Is it the same line or space?' and 'Am I still in the same bar?' If both are yes, the accidental still applies.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 4/4. Bar 1: F sharp, G, F, A. Bar 2: F, G, F, A.

steps: Tap the first F sharp, then the second F in bar 1. They sound the same: both are F sharp.
Now tap the F in bar 2. It is lower: the sharp has stopped at the bar-line.
Compare the two F notes in bar 2: no sign, so both are plain F.
demonstration.textAlternative: Two bars; in bar 1 an F sharp is followed by another F that is also sharp, and in bar 2 the F is plain.

guided.prompt: How many notes in bar 2 sound as G♯?

music.textAlternative: treble clef, 4/4. Bar 1: a note on the 2nd line with a sharp sign, a note on the 3rd line, a note in the 2nd space, a note on a ledger line below the stave. Bar 2: a note on the 2nd line, a note in the 2nd space, a note on a ledger line below the stave, a note on a ledger line below the stave.

1.reason: An accidental only lasts to the end of its own bar. In the next bar the note goes back to what the key signature says.

hints: An accidental lasts to the end of the bar.
An accidental lasts until the end of the bar, on its own line or space. A natural sign cancels it. A new bar starts afresh.

feedback.correct: An accidental lasts to the end of the bar.

mistakes.accidental-forgotten: An accidental keeps working for the rest of the bar on that line or space.
mistakes.accidental-carried-over-barline: A bar-line cancels accidentals — unless the note is tied across it.
mistakes.key-signature-ignored: Don't forget the key signature: it affects every note with that letter name.
mistakes.different-octave-assumed: An accidental only affects notes on the same line or space — not the same letter in another octave.
mistakes.tie-over-barline: A tie carries the accidental into the next bar, but only for the tied note.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Go through the bar from the start, tracking each accidental.
